title: Or is reprobation only by foresight of final unbelief — Lutherans deny the former, affirm the latter
pass_a_gloss: Or, rather, is no reprobation given except according to foresight of final impenitence and unbelief, and of this as the sole cause of reprobation as considered in the decree — while to all so foreseen sufficient means have been granted for faith and repentance, and also for salvation? The Lutherans deny the former; they affirm the latter. Against the Reformed.
pass_b_english: Or is there no reprobation at all except according to foresight of final impenitence and unbelief, treated as the one cause of reprobation inside the decree — while those so foreseen have all been granted means enough for faith and repentance, and for salvation too?
The Lutherans deny the first account and affirm this second one. The Reformed stand against that.
source_text: An verò Reprobatio nulla detur, nisi secundùm praescientiam finalis impaenitentiae, & incredulitatis, & hujus tanquam causae unicae Reprobationis consideratae in Decreto; dùm fuerint omnibus ità praescitis sufficientia ad fidem & resipiscentiam, tum & ad salutem concessa media? Prius negant, post. affirm. Luth. Contra Reform.

lemmas.gloss: deny the former; affirm the latter

notes: Controv. print p. 50-51 / PDF ~151. Closing Affirm/Neg of Controv. VI question pair.
